newsitem.title: NORWAY: Large share block traded in Storebrand.
newsitem.headline: Large share block traded in Storebrand.

text.p: Share trading in Norway's biggest insurer Storebrand ASA was again hectic on Friday with a large block of five million preference shares moving in one sale.
Trade has been heavy in Storebrand since it announced plans on Wednesday to merge with the country's second largest bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.

On Thursday billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke raised his stake in Storebrand to 10 percent, making him one of the largest shareholders along with New York-based hedging fund Tiger Management Corp and food-based conglomerate Orkla, which both hold around 10 percent.
Market sources said state pension fund, Folketrygdfondet, was the likely buyer of the block, which was sold by charity foundation Stiftelsen UNI.

The block moved at 0759 GMT at a price of 13.50 crowns. At 1034 GMT Storebrand's preference share stood 0.30 crowns down at 13.00 crowns in turnover of 70 million crowns, while the ordinary stock had slipped 0.10 crowns to 46.40 crowns.
Folketrygdfondet's holding in Storebrand before the acquisition was 7,816,958 shares, or 7.81 percent. The fund declined to make any comment on its shareholding.
Market players and the media have speculated that Storebrand's major shareholders are either moving to block the proposed fusion or are shuffling for position on the board of the new merged company.
